stem:
Chitra has a paper cut-out of a capital letter S. She wants to decide whether it has line symmetry and whether it has rotational symmetry.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Answer "rotational symmetry" alone, naming that label instead of running both tests.
Decide from a single glance that whatever is true of one kind of symmetry is automatically true of the other.
Apply the fold test for line symmetry and the turn test for rotational symmetry separately; the letter may have one, both, or neither.
Pick the answer from the printed word "letter" in the stem, without folding or turning the cut-out.

teacher.key_rationale: Line symmetry and rotational symmetry are independent: fold and rotate separately. A figure can have either, both, or neither. Naming one label, tying the two tests together, or grabbing a printed word all miss that independence.
